title: Timing GPU code
summary: Why a naive timer reports a matmul as almost free.

choices.text: The matmul was cached from an earlier call, so PyTorch skipped it.
`time.time()` cannot measure anything below a millisecond, so it rounds down.
Python's `@` operator runs on the CPU, and the GPU work starts only at `c.cpu()`.
The kernel launch is asynchronous: the timer measured queuing the work, not running it.
